pages.title: VOWEL TEAMS
pages.subtitle: PHONICS SKILL 1 · LONG VOWEL PATTERNS · TEACH

blocks.text: VOWEL TEAMS  PHONICS SKILL 1 · LONG VOWEL PATTERNS

• ai/ay — first vowel talks, second is silent: rain, day
  • ee/ea — tree, read, team, clean
  • oa/ow — boat, snow, road, grow
  • ay and ow usually end a word; ai and oa usually sit in the middle

blocks.text: VOWEL TEAMS ASSESSMENT  PHONICS SKILL 1 · LONG VOWEL PATTERNS · SHOW WHAT YOU KNOW

Fill in the blank: Choose a word from the bank that fits, then read the full sentence aloud.

1. The ______ ran across the yard.   2. We will ______ tomorrow.   3. It felt very ______.

4. She began to ______ the letter.   5. The sky turned ______ before the storm.

Quick review:

  • ai/ay = long a
  • ee/ea = long e
  • oa/ow = long o

pages.title: R-CONTROLLED VOWELS
pages.subtitle: PHONICS SKILL 2 · THE BOSSY R · TEACH

blocks.text: R-CONTROLLED VOWELS  PHONICS SKILL 2 · THE BOSSY R

• ar — car, farm, shark, star
  • er/ir/ur — her, bird, hurt (all sound alike!)
  • or — corn, storm, fork, short
  • When a vowel meets r, it is no longer short or long — it makes its own sound

blocks.text: DIPHTHONGS  PHONICS SKILL 3 · GLIDING VOWEL SOUNDS

• oi/oy — coin, toy (mouth glides)
  • ou/ow — cloud, cow
  • au/aw — haul, paw
  • oy and aw usually end a word; oi and au usually sit in the middle

blocks.text: SILENT LETTERS  PHONICS SKILL 4 · TRICKY CONSONANTS

• kn (silent k) — knee, know, knife
  • wr (silent w) — write, wrist, wrap
  • mb (silent b) — comb, thumb, climb
  • gh (silent gh) — light, night, high

pages.title: PREFIXES & SUFFIXES
pages.subtitle: PHONICS SKILL 5 · WORD PARTS · TEACH

blocks.text: PREFIXES & SUFFIXES  PHONICS SKILL 5 · WORD PARTS

• Prefixes go at the front: un- (not), re- (again), dis- (opposite)
  • Suffixes go at the end: -ing, -ed, -ly, -ful, -tion
  • Cover the prefix/suffix, read the root word first, then add the parts back

pages.title: SYLLABLE DIVISION
pages.subtitle: DECODING SKILL 1 · BREAK IT DOWN · TEACH

blocks.text: SYLLABLE DIVISION  DECODING SKILL 1 · BREAK IT DOWN

• Closed syllable — ends in a consonant, short vowel: rab·bit
  • Open syllable — ends in a vowel, long vowel: ti·ger
  • VC/CV pattern — split between two middle consonants: nap·kin
  • Find the vowels first, then decide where to split between them

pages.title: STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS
pages.subtitle: DECODING SKILL 2 · WORD DETECTIVE · TEACH

blocks.text: STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS  DECODING SKILL 2 · WORD DETECTIVE

• Find the root word first — the main meaning
  • Peel off any prefix at the start
  • Peel off any suffix at the end
  • Example: un·happi·ly = un (not) + happy + ly (in a way)

pages.title: GLOSSARY
pages.subtitle: KEY VOCABULARY FROM EVERY UNIT

blocks.text: Glossary  KEY VOCABULARY FROM EVERY UNIT

cells.text: Two vowels together that spell one long vowel sound (ai, ee, oa)
A vowel followed by r that makes its own special sound
Two vowels that glide together into one new sound (oi, ow)
A letter that is written but not heard (kn, wr, mb, gh)
A word part added to the front of a root word
A word part added to the end of a root word
The main word part that carries the core meaning
A syllable that ends in a consonant with a short vowel
A syllable that ends in a vowel with a long vowel sound
A word chunk with exactly one vowel sound

blocks.text: Answer Key & Scoring Guide  TEACHER REFERENCE

How to use this book: Each unit’s Assessment page has a matching table — check answers against the Word Bank table on that unit’s Teach page. Every pattern label (ai, ar, oi, kn, un-, closed, etc.) is shown in bold at the start of its Word Bank row.

Scoring guide: 9–10 correct = Mastered · 7–8 correct = Proficient, review word bank · Below 7 = Reteach unit before moving on.
